claim: Gene-expression profiles allow the two classes to be told apart in new samples: the classification error rate is at most 0.40.

data_keys.meaning: expression level of each gene in each sample
True for a sample of class B, False for a sample of class A

claim: The laboratory values in X predict the outcome y for new patients: the R-squared of a ridge regression of y on the 20 laboratory values (penalty 1.0 on standardised values, with an intercept) is at least 0.10.

data_keys.meaning: 20 laboratory values per patient; a value that was not measured for a patient is NaN
continuous clinical outcome of each patient

claim: Baseline BMI explains at least 10% of the variance in the change in BMI between baseline and follow-up (R-squared of at least 0.10).

data_keys.meaning: BMI of each child at the baseline visit, in kg/m2
a second BMI measurement of each child at the baseline visit, in kg/m2
BMI of each child at the follow-up visit five years after baseline, in kg/m2

claim: Fourteen pregnant dams each had a measured exposure level to a chemical, and 4 pups per dam were scored on a performance test at weaning. Claim: across dams, the correlation between a dam's exposure level and the mean score of her pups is positive, judged by a one-sided test of the correlation against zero at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: exposure level of each dam
performance score at weaning of each pup of each dam

claim: At a given height, the mean forced vital capacity of smokers and of non-smokers differs by at least 0.2 L: the difference between the two group means, after accounting for height, is at least 0.2 L in absolute value.

data_keys.meaning: forced vital capacity of each subject, in litres
standing height of each subject, in cm
True if the subject is a current smoker

claim: Sensor measurements classify the disease status of newly recruited subjects: the area under the ROC curve of the classification is at least 0.70.

data_keys.meaning: sensor measurements of each recording of each subject
True if the subject has the disease

claim: In 400 adults with systolic blood pressure measured at five annual visits, those with a higher initial blood pressure have a lower yearly rate of change: the regression slope of an individual's underlying yearly rate of change in systolic blood pressure on the individual's underlying initial systolic blood pressure is at most -0.03 mmHg per year per mmHg.

data_keys.meaning: systolic blood pressure of each individual at each of five annual visits, with the visits in time order, in mmHg

claim: Heart weight accounts for at least 10% of the variance in liver weight beyond what body mass accounts for: the increase in R-squared when heart weight is added to a regression of liver weight on body mass is at least 0.10.

data_keys.meaning: liver weight of each mouse, in g
heart weight of each mouse, in g
body mass of each mouse, in g

claim: In a field experiment, 8 plots were each surveyed on 12 successive dates and scored as occupied or not by a species on each date; the array fenced marks plots fenced against grazers. Claim: mean occupancy is higher in fenced plots than in open plots by at least 0.15, where the occupancy of a plot is the fraction of dates on which it is occupied, and a one-sided test of the difference between the mean occupancy of fenced plots and that of open plots is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: True if the species was present in that plot on that date; dates are in time order
True if the plot was fenced against grazers

claim: A second-order polynomial regression of the quality score y on the process readings X (an intercept, the 10 readings, their squares and all pairwise products, fitted by ordinary least squares) predicts y for new runs with a Pearson correlation between predicted and observed y of at least 0.30.

data_keys.meaning: 10 continuous process readings recorded for each production run
continuous quality score of each production run

claim: Across 2000 adult specimens of one beetle species, head width and wing length are associated beyond what body length explains: the partial correlation between head width and wing length, controlling for body length, is at least 0.30.

data_keys.meaning: head width of each specimen, in mm
wing length of each specimen, in mm
body length of each specimen, in mm

claim: Gene-expression profiles allow tumour tissue to be distinguished from normal tissue in new samples: the classification error rate is at most 0.20.

data_keys.meaning: log expression level of each gene in each tissue sample
True for a tumour tissue sample, False for a normal tissue sample
